abstract: Egon Zehnder's 2025 survey of CFOs reveals that artificial intelligence is transforming finance functions by accelerating decision-making and enabling shifts from transactional to strategic work. While fewer than 10% of finance leaders have fully integrated AI across their functions, 18% have already eliminated roles due to AI implementation, with the heaviest cuts in accounting (88%), FP&A (38%), and treasury (33%). CFOs view AI as crucial to both financial performance and broader enterprise strategy, anticipating a shift toward human-led, AI-enabled finance teams focused on creating value rather than executing routine tasks.
keyFindings: 18% of CFOs have already eliminated roles due to AI, with 88% of cuts occurring in accounting, 38% in FP&A, and 33% in treasury.
Fewer than 10% of finance leaders surveyed have fully integrated or scaled AI accounting and finance use cases across their functions and organizations.
Nearly all CFOs surveyed believe machine learning and AI will have the greatest impact on the future of the finance function.
CFOs expect AI to enable finance experts to shift from transactional tasks to strategic influence and create deeper business partnerships.
Finance teams are experiencing the earliest white-collar AI displacement compared to other corporate functions.
methodology: Survey of CFOs conducted by Egon Zehnder in 2025, following up on respondents from their 2024 report on evolving CFO responsibilities. The survey explored AI adoption levels, areas of value creation, and team-building strategies. Specific sample size, geographic scope, and industry breakdown not detailed in the available excerpt.
qualifiers: The source notes that AI adoption is 'still in the early stages of implementation.' The article is a summary of findings with the full report available for download, suggesting the complete methodology and detailed limitations may be contained in the full report. Geographic scope and industry representation of the survey sample not specified in the excerpt provided.
